long_biography.plain_text:
Martha Rivers Ingram's involvement in Nashville's cultural life began well before she led her family's distribution businesses. Raised in Charleston, South Carolina, she studied history at Vassar and worked in her father's radio and television company, including a classical-music programme. In Nashville she helped establish the Tennessee Performing Arts Center and remained a sustained supporter of the symphony, opera and repertory theatre.

She joined Ingram Industries in public affairs and succeeded her husband Bronson as chair after his death. The family separated its computer-distribution arm as Ingram Micro, while retaining book distribution and inland marine transport within the group. As chair of Vanderbilt University's trustees, she helped shape its residential-college plans and supported the Blair School of Music.
